newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria 1996 new car sales seen down 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria 1996 new car sales seen down 30 pct.

text.p: Sales of new cars in Bulgaria are expected to fall by around 30 percent this year while second-hand car sales should remain steady as the market continued to shrink, the car importers union said on Friday.
"I expect a more than 30 percent decline in new car sales this year," the head of the car importers union Boris Marekov told Reuters.
Car sales by authorised Western car dealers for the first 11 months of this year amounted to around 7,000, down on 11,500 in 1995 and 13,107 in 1994.
This compares to some 70,000 imported second-hand cars sold in 1996 and some 60,000 sold last year, said Marekov.
Police say most of the imported second-hand cars are stolen and therefore are sold at much lower prices.

High import taxes, a further four percent rise in value added tax to 22 percent this year and a drastic depreciation of the local currency have pushed new car prices higher, making them practically unsellable, car dealers said.
"Lack of incentives for importers of new cars leads to a hazardous ageing of Bulgaria's cars," said Marekov.
The average age of some 90 percent of the cars driven in Bulgaria, mostly Soviet-made Ladas and Moskviches, is around 20 years, statistics show.
Prospects are less than bright as an unprecedented economic crisis caused by delayed market reforms has shrunk private businesses and reduced the buying power of the average Bulgarian.
A car-making joint venture between Rover Group Ltd, a subsidiary of Bayerische Motoren Werke AG and a Bulgarian consortium, closed down in April amid complaints of a lack of government support.
